attributes.residual: NONE of the mode-compare class: a project-wide sweep confirms every `gGameMode <cmp> literal`, case arm, and assignment in src/ is now spelled as an e_mode name. Three categories are deliberately left raw, each for a named reason. (1) The `gGameMode & 0x8000` / `& 0x4000` FAMILY-BIT tests (player.c:716/861/1319/3257, message.c:724, gauntworld.c:1610/5059/6585, combat.c:2253) -- these classify a mode's FAMILY rather than compare against one mode, so no single enum constant is the right spelling; substituting one (MA_CREDITS happens to equal 0x8000) would assert a false identity. This continues wave 2's deliberate treatment of the same idiom at items.c:1256 and is the documented MA_/MG_ group idiom described in gamemode.h's own header comment. (2) game/audio/sndfx.c -- another lane owns it this run; note the inventory's own anomaly (a) still stands, its sndFxInit assigns a POINTER into `gGameMode` while sndFxPaused() reads it as a mode, so that symbol is very likely misattributed and should NOT be respelled before the identity is settled. (3) DECIMAL literals below 0x4000: my converter refuses these by design, because the ungrouped M_* ids are small integers and a bare `4` could equally be an unrelated count or index -- auto-respelling it would invent meaning. Grouped ids (>= 0x4000) are unambiguous in any base, which is exactly what made tower.c's decimal 16400 and auxscreen.c's 16398/16399 safe. No such small-decimal site was found in any TU I own.
